description: Generalist gripper next stage: build the attachment. It is simply a small, black, flat piece that slides into the gripper and has two slots for loops (straps). Closely reference the reference images — key photo cad/reference/generalist_gripper_gen6_closed.png, plus the other references under cad/reference and references/generalist. Model it in OpenSCAD alongside the current gripper (Gen 16, Two Finger Gripper/versions/v016_generalist_rounded_point). Make every piece separable: each part its own module and its own exported STL, viewable individually and together in the live preview. Use the repo's dual-render workflow (cad/compare: three.js vision render + OpenSCAD STL, same angles, diffed; STL is truth).

results.identified_issue: Read 'slides into the gripper' as a dovetail rail on a lug fused to the finger's outer edge (rail_p = two traced outline points at z 12.8 and 36.3; the edge is within 0.2 mm of that line). I could not cut the groove into the finger itself because the honeycomb holes come within about 1.7 mm of the outer edge. The groove's open end is at the tip, because entering from the base would hit the J-hook. I read 'two slots for loops' as one loop straddling the digit (the classic two-slot strap mount). If Jake meant two separate loops (for example thumb and index), change slot_gap and slot_wall or the slot layout in gripper.scad. A first square T groove was swapped for a 45 degree dovetail so it prints without support. Constant thickness: side_taper, half_thick, tip_thick and dot_z were removed. The concept.json keys changed (rail, lug, slide, strap_slots). Not verified: any print or fit, the strap and digit sizes, and retention against sliding toward the tip (there is no detent).
results.summary: New Gen 17: Gen 16's fingers at full thickness to the point, plus a black flat strap slide with two loop slots that slides into a dovetail on each finger. Old Gen 17 removed.
results.detailed_description:
I replaced the old Gen 17 (v017_generalist_simple, with its pads and camera cradle) with v017_generalist_strap_slide. There is no camera.

Fingers: Gen 16's shape, holes, grooves and closed tip contact, unchanged. They are now the full 12 mm thick from base to point. I removed Gen 16's side taper, so the point exists only in the closing plane. previews/edge.png shows a finger edge-on.

Attachment: I added a small yellow lug to each finger's outer edge, mid-shank, where the edge is straight. It has a dovetail groove that is closed at the base end. The black strap slide is a flat 3.5 mm plate, 28 x 37 mm, with a matching dovetail tongue. Slide it down from the tip end until it hits the stop. It has two 21 x 3.5 mm slots for 20 mm webbing, 24 mm apart. Your digit lies under the plate between them, and the loop goes down one slot, around the digit and up the other. I made the dovetail all 45 degree faces so the finger prints flat without support. Print the slide standing on its end.

Every piece is its own module and STL: left and right finger, left and right slide. The viewer shows them alone or together, and the slides open and close with their fingers. The three.js vision and the STL renders overlap 95 to 100 percent. The only gap is the tongue, which only the STL has (previews/compare_web_stl.png).

All checks pass: watertight single bodies; 33 holes in the finger and 2 in the slide; Gen 16's tip contact (only the points touch, 20.7 degrees); the slide clears its finger but catches if pulled outboard; no slide hits the other side over 0 to 30 degrees; the finger is 12 mm thick all the way to the point.

Things to judge: the 20 mm strap width, the 24 mm digit gap, the 0.2 mm fit and the lug position are my guesses, not measurements. Nothing stops the slide sliding back out toward the tip except friction, so it may want a snap once it is printed. Nothing is printed yet.

results.notes: Scope change from Jake (supersedes earlier messages): versioning is now 1.x = gripper only, 2.x = gripper plus handles (strap loops); old Gen N = 1.N. This pebble now covers ONLY version 1.17: the gripper fingers keep the same thickness along their whole length (no narrowing to a point in the thickness direction; the point is only in the closing plane), replacing the unrigged current Gen 17 (v017_generalist_simple). Leave the loop attachment out — it moves to a separate 2.1 pebble that builds on 1.17. See AGENTS.md for the versioning scheme.

Updates from Jake: (1) This is Gen 17. Replace the current Gen 17 (Two Finger Gripper/versions/v017_generalist_simple — effectively the old Gen 16) because it isn't really rigged. (2) No camera attachment. Scope is only how the loops (straps) attach to the gripper: the flat black slide-in piece with two loop slots. (3) The gripper fingers keep the same thickness along their whole length — they must not narrow to a point in the thickness direction; the point is only in the closing plane.

summary: Model a Gen 17 OpenSCAD attachment replacing the old v017: a flat black slide-in piece with two strap loop slots, no camera. Fingers keep constant thickness and taper to a point only in the closing plane.
